speaker: SPEAKER_02
transcript: A lot has changed, but a lot has stayed the same. I was elected to Congress in 98, and I'm the 20th African-American woman elected since Congress. I had this first session. And that's outrageous. And so to change the institution and the culture of Congress, where I am, is very difficult. But because of Shirley Chisholm, they can't ignore us. And they're about 21 members now in the CBC who are black women. And so that's a big shift. But when it comes to the issues that we champion, It's always an uphill battle. For example, we wanted an arch caucus poverty to be a big issue, people living below the poverty line and those who are low income and struggling. And for years and years and years, I tried to be the voice to get more of our members engaged in talking about not only fighting for the middle class, but fighting for people who are poor and low income and the most vulnerable. Well now, I chair the WIPS Task Force on Poverty, Income and Equality and Opportunity, and we have a hundred members. But it took a heck of a lot. And so while a lot has changed, it still takes a lot to break through as an African-American woman.
